ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

The present appeal is filed by the appellant - Insurance Company under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, being NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3853/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 21.2.2007 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Vadodara in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1185 of 1995, by which, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding Rs.3,73,400/- with 9% p.a. from the date of application till 2000 December and at the rate of 9% from 2001 January till realization, to be paid to claimant/s, by holding opponents liable, jointly and severally.

sentences.text:
2. The facts of the present appeal are as under :
2.1

The claimant filed the claim petition stating that on 16.12.94 at about 9.30 hours in the morning, was going on walk from his village Kamlapura via Rampura, when he reached Moti Bhadol village, at that time, the opponent no.1 came with his tractor number GJ.6A.8261 and tractor trolley no.GJ.6T.7693 and dashed with the appellant because of which he sustained injuries.
Therefore, the complaint came to be filed from the hospital against the opponent no.1
2.2 The notices were served to the opponents.
Opponent no.1-driver did not file any reply.
However, the opponent no.2-insurance company filed the written statement against the claim petition.
The issues were framed by the Tribunal.
Oral as well as documentary evidence were led NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3853/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined before the Tribunal.
After hearing the submissions made by the rival parties, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition(s) and awarded compensation as noted above.
2.3 Hence, the insurance company has filed the present appeal before this Court.

3. Learned advocate for the appellant - Insurance Company has submitted that though the claimant has not placed any cogent proof of income, the learned Tribunal has awarded the amount, which is on higher side and therefore prayed to allow this petition.
4. Per contra, learned advocate for the respondent no.1-claimant has submitted that the award amount is just and proper and the income which is considered is proper.
Even on the rate of interest, he has submitted that the same is just and proper and therefore, no interference is called for.
He, therefore, requested that this petition be dismissed.
No appearance is filed for the respondent no.2-original driver.
5. I have considered the submissions made by the respective parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

I have also considered the pleadings NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3853/2007 JUDGMENT DATED:
15/07/2024 undefined of the parties before the Tribunal.
The accident, the cause of accident and the involvement of the tractor and trolley in the accident is not in dispute.

It is also not in dispute that the claimant suffered injuries in the said vehicular accident and he had to take treatment and had United India Insurance Co.Ltd vs Jagdishbhai Lallubhai Patel on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7436902/
2 suffered partial permanent disability in the said accident.

sentences.text: As regards the income, the learned Tribunal has considered that the claimant was an agriculturist, he suffered loss of income due to the accident and considering the prospective income, loss of income and the disability, has awarded the compensation, as noted hereinabove.
6. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of `just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of `just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavour should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3853/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined 7.
Considering the above principle, this Court is of the opinion that the learned Tribunal has awarded compensation which is just and proper and not required to be interfered with.
8. In view of above ,the following order is passed.
8.1 The present appeal is dismissed with no order as to costs.

8.2 The amount lying with the Tribunal and/or in the FDR, pursuant to the order of this Court if any, shall be disbursed to the claimant, along with accrued interest thereon if any, by account payee cheque/RTGS/NEFT, after proper verification and after following due procedure, within a period of six weeks from today.
8.3 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.

(SANDEEP N. BHATT,J) SRILATHA United India Insurance Co.Ltd vs Jagdishbhai Lallubhai Patel on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7436902/
